The ego vehicle is traveling at 30 kph (approx. 8.33 m/s) with a visibility range of 21 m. A static obstacle is located at x=29.6 m, which is beyond the current visibility range (29.6 > 21). The stopping distance for 30 kph is typically around 15-20 m (depending on reaction time and friction), which is less than the distance to the obstacle. However, since the obstacle is not yet visible, the primary immediate action in a visibility-limited scenario where a hazard is known to exist ahead but is currently obscured is to maintain a safe speed or prepare to stop if it becomes visible. Given the options usually map to: A0 (No Action/Cruise), A1 (Accelerate), A2 (Decelerate/Brake), A3 (Lane Change Left), A4 (Lane Change Right), A6 (Stop). Since the obstacle is static and ahead, and we are approaching it, deceleration is the safest proactive measure to ensure we can stop if the obstacle is confirmed or if visibility worsens, although strictly speaking, if we can see it's 29.6m away
